sources.entry: django-guardian - Implementation of per-object permissions for Django.

summary.one_liner: django-guardian adds per-object permissions to Django's authorization system, so users can be granted rights on individual model instances rather than only globally.
summary.what_it_does: It plugs into Django's built-in auth framework as an extra authentication backend, letting you check permissions like has_perm on a specific object. The assign_perm shortcut grants a permission to a user or group for one object, and the has_perm check then reflects that per-object grant. Global permissions remain unaffected, so a user granted change rights on one group does not gain them everywhere. The README also describes a GuardedModelAdmin class that replaces the standard Django admin ModelAdmin to add object-level permission support in the admin panel. A contrib module provides integration with django-unfold.
use_cases: restrict editing of individual records to specific users
per-object access control in Django admin
grant a user change rights on one object only
row-level permissions in a Django web app
share a single item with a particular user or group
how_to_run: Use guardian.shortcuts.assign_perm to grant object permissions, and replace admin.ModelAdmin with GuardedModelAdmin for admin support
notable: Per-object permissions layered on Django's standard authorization backend
GuardedModelAdmin replaces ModelAdmin for object-level permissions in the admin
assign_perm shortcut for granting object permissions
caveats: The README does not state any caveats or platform limits.
Requires adding a database migration step to create guardian tables.
